defect_1_self_proving_cyclic_digest.before: source_cyclic_order_sha256 and projected_cyclic_order_sha256 were both _cyclic_digest(loops) over the SAME topological PhysicalEdgeId walk of the source faces
defect_1_self_proving_cyclic_digest.why_no_violation_can_be_built: the projection is a map on vertex POSITIONS; the cyclic sequence of physical edges around a boundary loop is a fact of face incidence, which no position map can permute. The pair could not differ on any input.
defect_1_self_proving_cyclic_digest.chosen_fork: removed from the proof claim, kept as a one-sided fingerprint
defect_1_self_proving_cyclic_digest.field_now: boundary_cyclic_order_sha256 (single field, recomputed by the validator)
defect_1_self_proving_cyclic_digest.outcome_now: NEAR_PLANAR_PROJECTION_CYCLIC_ORDER_CHANGED retired, enum member kept (removing it would break two released schemas non-additively)
where_the_geometry_went: NEAR_PLANAR_PROJECTION_FAN_IDENTITY_CHANGED - rotation system computed independently on the source chart and on the projected chart
defect_1_self_proving_cyclic_digest.executable_demonstration: test_the_boundary_cyclic_fingerprint_cannot_depend_on_the_projection - two certificates over the same faces and wildly different charts (one folded) carry the identical fingerprint

measured_disagreement.method: every live build_projection_embedding_certificate call across test_embedding_certificates, test_near_planar_policy, test_near_planar_snapshot_validation, test_planar_metric_v2

after_the_new_negative_fixtures.note: the 2 prefix mismatches are the two deliberate collapse fixtures

measured_disagreement.explanation: every mismatch on the base fixture set differs only in the THIRD basis vertex: a near-planar projection is entitled to make an almost-collinear triple exactly collinear, which is the point of the projection. Requiring full tuple equality would reject legitimate product fixtures - which is exactly why the previous branch collapsed both sides into one value instead.

defect_2_self_proving_anchor.what_remains_a_refusal: a mismatch of the PREFIX (origin, first). Its only cause is two DISTINCT source vertices landing on one chart point, which is a real injectivity failure.
negative_fixtures: test_projection_anchor_prefix_change_names_a_collapsed_interior_vertex - an INTERIOR vertex collapses, boundary-occurrence injectivity stays silent, the prefix and the new all-vertex injectivity check do not
test_the_two_anchor_laws_disagree_on_a_live_patch_and_it_is_not_a_refusal - the two tuples differ and the record is still admitted

test_validator_recomputes_the_two_formerly_self_proving_claims[source_anchor_vertex_ids] - overwriting the source anchor with the OLD self-proving value (a copy of the projected anchor) is rejected by the validator

defect_3_interior_injectivity.before: boundary and orientation were certified; nothing checked whether the chart covers a point twice
defect_3_interior_injectivity.authority: exact ear-clipping triangulation of every projected face polygon + AABB broad phase + exact separating-axis test over all triangle pairs
premises_recorded_on_the_way: coincident_projected_vertex_pair_count - ALL vertices, not only boundary occurrences
nonsimple_projected_face_count - each face polygon must admit an ear-clipped triangulation, i.e. must be a simple non-degenerate polygon
projected_face_triangle_count, triangle_pair_broadphase_test_count, triangle_pair_exact_test_count - the cost is recorded, not asserted
defect_3_interior_injectivity.why_fan_triangulation_was_rejected: a fan from the first vertex of a legitimate non-convex face produces triangles outside the face and would report a false overlap with its neighbour
defect_3_interior_injectivity.why_ear_clipping_is_a_proof_not_a_heuris: by the two-ears theorem every simple polygon with four or more vertices has an ear, so a stalled clip is evidence of non-simplicity

adversarial_fixture.name: test_projection_names_an_interior_overlap_a_simple_boundary_hides
adversarial_fixture.shape: strip of three quads; the two INTERNAL edges b1-t1 and b2-t2 cross, so the middle face is a bowtie
adversarial_fixture.overlap_witness: (61/4, 59/2) is strictly inside face q0 AND strictly inside face q2; q0 and q2 share no vertex
adversarial_fixture.why_the_boundary_test_missed_it: the crossing edges are INTERNAL; new_nonadjacent_edge_intersection_count scans boundary occurrences only
adversarial_fixture.why_the_area_sign_missed_it: a bowtie subtracts its lobes, so the signed area of the middle face stays positive

finding_reported_as_a_discovery.statement: with the FULL premise set - simple pairwise non-crossing boundary loops with correct nesting and orientation PLUS simple positively oriented face polygons - interior overlap is impossible: the covering multiplicity of a point equals the winding number of the oriented boundary about it, which is 0 or 1.
finding_reported_as_a_discovery.consequence: the direct pairwise authority cannot produce a violation that the premise set would not also produce. It was still built, because it derives nothing from that theorem.
finding_reported_as_a_discovery.the_gap_that_did_exist: face-polygon simplicity was NOT a premise the old certificate checked, which is exactly why the adversarial fixture exists and passed

interior_authority_cost.method: square grid patch of quads, exact Fractions, ear clipping + AABB broad phase + exact separating axis
